    {"id": "c1", "name": "OpenAPI Specification (OAS)", "aliases": ["OAS"], "description": "A standard, programming language-agnostic interface description for HTTP APIs.", "grounding_span": "The OpenAPI Specification (OAS) defines a standard, programming language-agnostic interface description for HTTP APIs", "location": "preamble"},
    {"id": "c2", "name": "OpenAPI Description (OAD)", "aliases": ["OAD"], "description": "A formal description of an API surface and semantics, possibly across multiple documents.", "grounding_span": "An **OpenAPI Description** (**OAD**) formally describes the surface of an API and its semantics.", "location": "§4.1.2"},
    {"id": "c3", "name": "entry document", "aliases": [], "description": "The document containing the OpenAPI Object where parsing of a multi-document OAD begins.", "grounding_span": "the document containing the OpenAPI Object where parsing begins is known as that OAD’s **entry document**", "location": "§4.1.2"},
    {"id": "c4", "name": "embedding format", "aliases": [], "description": "Another format in which an OpenAPI Object may be embedded.", "grounding_span": "An OpenAPI Object *MAY* be embedded in another format, called the **embedding format**", "location": "§4.1.2"},
    {"id": "c5", "name": "multi-document OAD", "aliases": [], "description": "An OAD distributed across multiple connected documents.", "grounding_span": "be distributed across multiple documents that are connected by various fields using URI references and implicit connections", "location": "§4.1.2"},
    {"id": "c6", "name": "undefined behavior", "aliases": [], "description": "Situations likely to produce outcomes contradicting the specification.", "grounding_span": "Behavior described as *undefined* is likely, at least in some circumstances, to result in outcomes that contradict the specification.", "location": "§2.2"},
    {"id": "c7", "name": "implementation-defined behavior", "aliases": [], "description": "Ambiguous requirements where implementations choose among compliant approaches.", "grounding_span": "Behavior described as *implementation-defined* allows implementations to choose which of several different-but-compliant approaches to a requirement to implement.", "location": "§2.2"},
    {"id": "c8", "name": "OAS versioning and feature set", "aliases": [], "description": "major.minor.patch versioning where major.minor designates the feature set.", "grounding_span": "The `major`.`minor` portion of the version string (for example `3.1`) *SHALL* designate the OAS feature set.", "location": "§2.1"},
    {"id": "c9", "name": "deprecation", "aliases": [], "description": "Fields/features marked Deprecated remain usable but should be replaced.", "grounding_span": "Certain fields or features may be marked **Deprecated**.", "location": "§2.1"},
    {"id": "c10", "name": "specification extensions", "aliases": ["x- extensions"], "description": "Patterned fields prefixed by x- to extend the specification.", "grounding_span": "The extensions properties are implemented as patterned fields that are always prefixed by `x-`.", "location": "§5"},
    {"id": "c11", "name": "fixed and patterned fields", "aliases": [], "description": "Two kinds of OAS object fields: declared-name and declared-pattern.", "grounding_span": "OAS Objects expose two types of fields: *fixed fields*, which have a declared name, and *patterned fields*, which have a declared pattern for the field name.", "location": "§3"},
    {"id": "c12", "name": "case sensitivity", "aliases": [], "description": "OAS field names are case-sensitive except where noted.", "grounding_span": "All field names in the specification are **case-sensitive**.", "location": "§3"},
    {"id": "c13", "name": "CommonMark rich text", "aliases": [], "description": "description fields support CommonMark markdown for rich text.", "grounding_span": "Throughout the specification `description` fields are noted as supporting [CommonMark] markdown formatting.", "location": "§3.3"},
    {"id": "c14", "name": "OpenAPI Object", "aliases": ["root object"], "description": "The root object of an OpenAPI Description.", "grounding_span": "This is the root object of the OpenAPI Description.", "location": "§4.1"},
    {"id": "c15", "name": "$self and base URI", "aliases": ["$self"], "description": "Self-assigned URI of a document that serves as its base URI.", "grounding_span": "The `$self` field provides the self-assigned URI of this document, which also serves as its base URI in accordance with [RFC3986] Section 5.1.1.", "location": "§4.1.1"},
    {"id": "c16", "name": "retrieval URI", "aliases": [], "description": "The most common base URI source when $self/$id is missing or relative.", "grounding_span": "The most common base URI source that is used in the event of a missing or relative `$self` (in the OpenAPI Object) and (for Schema Object) `$id` is the retrieval URI.", "location": "§4.1.2.2.1"},
    {"id": "c17", "name": "relative references (URIs vs URLs)", "aliases": [], "description": "Reference URIs resolved as identifiers, contrasted with API URLs.", "grounding_span": "are resolved as *identifiers*, and described by this specification as ***URIs***, in contrast with API URLs.", "location": "§4.1.2.2"},
    {"id": "c18", "name": "resolving implicit connections", "aliases": [], "description": "Non-URI-based connections between parts of an OAD.", "grounding_span": "Several features of this specification require resolution of non-URI-based connections to some other part of the OpenAPI Description (OAD).", "location": "§4.1.2.3"},
    {"id": "c19", "name": "webhooks", "aliases": [], "description": "Incoming requests initiated by the API provider that a consumer may implement.", "grounding_span": "The incoming webhooks that *MAY* be received as part of this API", "location": "§4.1.1"},
    {"id": "c20", "name": "Info Object", "aliases": [], "description": "Metadata about the API.", "grounding_span": "The object provides metadata about the API.", "location": "§4.2"},

    {"id": "c23", "name": "Components Object", "aliases": [], "description": "Holder of reusable objects referenced from elsewhere.", "grounding_span": "Holds a set of reusable objects for different aspects of the OAS.", "location": "§4.7"},
    {"id": "c24", "name": "path templating", "aliases": [], "description": "Curly-brace template expressions marking replaceable URL path sections.", "grounding_span": "Path templating refers to the usage of template expressions, delimited by curly braces (`{}`), to mark a section of a URL path as replaceable using path parameters.", "location": "§4.8.2"},

    {"id": "c27", "name": "parameter locations", "aliases": ["in"], "description": "Five parameter locations specified by the in field.", "grounding_span": "There are five possible parameter locations specified by the `in` field:", "location": "§4.12.1"},
    {"id": "c28", "name": "style-based serialization", "aliases": ["style", "explode"], "description": "Style values that define how parameter values are serialized.", "grounding_span": "In order to support common ways of serializing simple parameters, a set of `style` values are defined.", "location": "§4.12.3"},
    {"id": "c29", "name": "URL percent-encoding", "aliases": [], "description": "Percent-decoding/encoding rules for API URLs and form-urlencoded content.", "grounding_span": "All API URLs *MUST* successfully parse and percent-decode using [RFC3986] rules.", "location": "§4.12.4"},
    {"id": "c30", "name": "Request Body Object", "aliases": [], "description": "A single request body with content keyed by media type.", "grounding_span": "Describes a single request body.", "location": "§4.13"},
    {"id": "c31", "name": "Media Type Object", "aliases": [], "description": "Describes content structured according to a media type key.", "grounding_span": "Each Media Type Object describes content structured in accordance with the media type identified by its key.", "location": "§4.14"},
    {"id": "c32", "name": "sequential media type", "aliases": [], "description": "A media type consisting of a repeating structure with no envelope.", "grounding_span": "a *sequential media type* is defined as any media type that consists of a repeating structure, without any sort of header, footer, envelope, or other metadata in addition to the sequence.", "location": "§4.14.3.1"},
    {"id": "c33", "name": "streaming content and itemSchema", "aliases": ["itemSchema"], "description": "itemSchema applies per stream item to support streaming.", "grounding_span": "The `itemSchema` field is provided to support streaming use cases for sequential media types", "location": "§4.14.3.1.1"},

    {"id": "c35", "name": "Encoding Object", "aliases": [], "description": "A single encoding definition applied to a single value.", "grounding_span": "A single encoding definition applied to a single value", "location": "§4.15"},

    {"id": "c37", "name": "binary data (raw and encoded)", "aliases": [], "description": "OAS describes raw (unencoded) or encoded binary data.", "grounding_span": "The OAS can describe either *raw* or *encoded* binary data.", "location": "§4.24.4.3"},

    {"id": "c42", "name": "Link Object (design-time links)", "aliases": [], "description": "A possible design-time link between a response and other operations.", "grounding_span": "The Link Object represents a possible design-time link for a response.", "location": "§4.20"},

    {"id": "cl3", "claim_text": "If the JSON Schema differs from section 4, that section must be considered authoritative.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "If the JSON Schema differs from this section, then this section *MUST* be considered authoritative.", "location": "§4"},
    {"id": "cl4", "claim_text": "The OAS dialect schema id is https://spec.openapis.org/oas/3.1/dialect/base.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "The OpenAPI Schema Object dialect for this version of the specification is identified by the URI `https://spec.openapis.org/oas/3.1/dialect/base` (the “OAS dialect schema id”).", "location": "§4.24.1"},
    {"id": "cl5", "claim_text": "As of 2020, the implicit flow is about to be deprecated by OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "Please note that as of 2020, the implicit flow is about to be deprecated by OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice.", "location": "§4.27"},
    {"id": "cl6", "claim_text": "Tooling must detect and handle reference cycles to prevent resource exhaustion.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "Tooling must detect and handle cycles to prevent resource exhaustion.", "location": "§6.6"},
    {"id": "cl7", "claim_text": "The behavior of readOnly differs from that specified by version 3.0 of this specification.", "claim_type": "empirical", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "Note that the behavior of `readOnly` in particular differs from that specified by version 3.0 of this specification.", "location": "§4.24.5.2"},
    {"id": "cl8", "claim_text": "Implementations MUST map sequential media types into the JSON Schema data model as if values were an array in the same order.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "Implementations *MUST* support mapping sequential media types into the JSON Schema data model by treating them as if the values were in an array in the same order.", "location": "§4.14.3.1"},

    {"id": "cl11", "claim_text": "The Reference Object cannot be extended with additional properties, and any properties added SHALL be ignored.", "claim_type": "normative", "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion", "grounding_span": "This object cannot be extended with additional properties, and any properties added *SHALL* be ignored.", "location": "§4.23.1"},

    {"id": "pr1", "text": "It is RECOMMENDED that the entry document of an OAD be named openapi.json or openapi.yaml.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "It is *RECOMMENDED* that the entry document of an OAD be named `openapi.json` or `openapi.yaml`.", "location": "§4.1.2"},
    {"id": "pr2", "text": "To ensure interoperability, references MUST use the target document's $self URI if the $self field is present.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "To ensure interoperability, references *MUST* use the target document’s `$self` URI if the `$self` field is present.", "location": "§4.1.1"},
    {"id": "pr3", "text": "YAML version 1.2 is RECOMMENDED along with the additional constraints in RFC9512 Section 3.4.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "YAML version 1.2 is *RECOMMENDED* along with the additional constraints listed in [RFC9512] Section 3.4.", "location": "§3.1"},
    {"id": "pr4", "text": "It is RECOMMENDED that OpenAPI description authors explicitly set the dialect through $schema in such documents.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "it is *RECOMMENDED* that OpenAPI description authors explicitly set the dialect through `$schema` in such documents.", "location": "§4.24.7"},
    {"id": "pr5", "text": "Recommended for most use cases is Authorization Code Grant flow with PKCE.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "Recommended for most use cases is Authorization Code Grant flow with PKCE.", "location": "§4.27"},
    {"id": "pr6", "text": "For resolving Components/Tag names from a referenced document, it is RECOMMENDED that tools resolve from the entry document rather than the current document.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "it is *RECOMMENDED* that tools resolve from the entry document, rather than the current document.", "location": "§4.1.2.3"},
    {"id": "pr7", "text": "All implementations SHOULD allow users to provide documents with their intended retrieval URIs so references can be resolved as if retrievals were performed.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "tool", "grounding_span": "all implementations *SHOULD* allow users to provide documents with their intended retrieval URIs so that references can be resolved as if retrievals were performed.", "location": "§4.1.2.2.1"},
    {"id": "pr8", "text": "OpenAPI Description authors should use newer fields and features to replace deprecated ones whenever possible.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "OpenAPI Description authors should use newer fields and features documented to replace the deprecated ones whenever possible.", "location": "§2.1"},
    {"id": "pr9", "text": "It is the responsibility of tooling to appropriately sanitize the Markdown.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "tool", "grounding_span": "It is the responsibility of tooling to appropriately sanitize the Markdown.", "location": "§6.7"},
    {"id": "pr10", "text": "Because of the potential for name clashes, the operationRef syntax is preferred for multi-document OADs.", "as_of_date": "2025-09-19", "scope": "api", "grounding_span": "Because of the potential for name clashes, the `operationRef` syntax is preferred for multi-document OADs.", "location": "§4.20.1"}

    {"type": "mentions", "from_id": "openapi-specification-core", "to_id": "c1", "grounding_span": "The OpenAPI Specification (OAS) defines a standard, programming language-agnostic interface description for HTTP APIs", "location": "preamble"},

    {"type": "defines", "from_id": "openapi-specification-core", "to_id": "d1", "grounding_span": "An **OpenAPI Description** (**OAD**) formally describes the surface of an API and its semantics.", "location": "§4.1.2"},
